DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM

1. Scope and Definitions
Personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
The controller is the entity that determines the purposes of processing.
The processor processes personal data solely on the controller documented instructions.

2. Processing Purposes
Personal data is processed for the purpose of delivering the service.
Personal data is processed for the purpose of improving the service.
The processor shall not sell personal data to third parties.
Data is retained for 24 months after the end of the contract.

3. Security Measures
The processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures.
Personal data shall be encrypted in transit and at rest.
The processor shall notify the controller of any personal data breach within 48 hours.
Access to personal data shall be limited to authorised personnel.

4. Subprocessors
The controller gives general written authorisation for the use of subprocessors.
The processor shall inform the controller of any intended change of subprocessor.
The processor remains fully liable for the acts and omissions of its subprocessors.

5. International Transfers
Personal data shall not be transferred outside the European Economic Area.
Transfers outside the European Economic Area require appropriate safeguards.
The processor shall keep a record of all international transfers.

The controller gives general written authorisation for subprocessors.
The processor remains liable for the acts of its subprocessors.
Personal data may not be transferred outside the European Economic Area.

cases.rationale: The summary drops the 48 hour breach notification obligation, which is exactly what a security-obligations brief needs. This is the positive case.

input.purpose: Summarize the security obligations the processor has.

cases.rationale: The summary drops only the definition of personal data and the purpose clauses, which do not matter for a security-obligations brief. A detector that flags these is useless. This is the false-alarm control. The expected value accepts either outcome: the subprocessor-change notification duty is a governance obligation, and whether it counts as a security obligation for this brief is a judgement call. The case is retained as a recorded disagreement rather than being scored as a pass or a failure.
